A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FairDICE work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; the added checklist and shifted appendix labels do not prevent matching content.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 report original MO-Four-Room, Random MOMDP, and D4MORL experiments, supplemented by numerical examples and sensitivity analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix H adds original results comparing training on full and trajectory-filtered D4MORL datasets.

M1.justification: Equation (4) and Algorithm 1 retain the same welfare-regularized distribution correction, dual optimization, and weighted behavior cloning. Appendix F's explicit Soft-χ² formulas explain existing computations rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds a deliberately biased training-data scenario that excludes the central, balanced-preference region in five existing D4MORL domains. This changes represented behavioral coverage, while the environments, objectives, and expert/amateur categories remain unchanged.

E2.justification: BC(P), MODT(P), and MORvS(P) remain the continuous-control comparators, and the finite-domain comparisons are retained. Figures 4–5 correct missing '(P)' suffixes in legends; these are the same methods already described in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces filtering trajectories whose preference weights all fall between 0.4 and 0.6, removing 24.0–67.7% of trajectories. Appendix E.2 revises the reported amateur perturbation probability from 35% to 65% for most environments, while specifying 35% uniform-action sampling for MO-Swimmer. This documentation change does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix H/Table 4 adds one targeted robustness study asking whether FairDICE remains effective without balanced demonstrations, across five domains and both dataset qualities. Existing α, β, and implicit-weight sensitivity analyses remain; the former Appendix H becomes Appendix I.

E5.justification: Table 4 adds explicit mean-plus/minus reporting for full-dataset D4MORL scores previously presented as mean lines in Figure 4, alongside filtered-data results, and specifies five seeds. The meaning of ± is undefined. Existing Figure 2 confidence intervals and Figure 8 standard-error reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds full/filtered NSW results for ten domain-quality combinations. Expert MO-Walker2d changes from 11.534 ± 0.039 to 9.562 ± 1.161 after filtering, whereas amateur MO-Swimmer changes from 11.820 ± 0.005 to 11.819 ± 0.001. These compare data conditions within v2; the main benchmark findings remain stable.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, its proof, and the counterexample remain unchanged. Section 5.1 corrects the transition summation identity, but new parentheses place the utility term under a minus sign in an intermediate objective, inconsistent with the preceding Lagrangian and unchanged Equation (4). Appendix F also supplies explicit conjugate and inverse-derivative formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of direct offline nonlinear-welfare optimization, equivalence to appropriately weighted regularized linear MORL, and effective fairness-aware performance with minimal additional parameters.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds a specific explanation involving broken Bellman recursion and unsuitable TD targets. Appendix H newly interprets the filtering results as robustness to biased or sparse data, without addressing the pronounced expert MO-Walker2d decline. The existing nonconvex-scalarization and dataset-dependence limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds a code-repository pointer and explicit Soft-χ² computations, explaining that no inner maximization loop is required. Appendix E.2 newly specifies the Unif(0.35, 1.65) action-scaling range and MO-Swimmer exception. Architecture, optimizer, hardware, and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The same 33 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against online fairness-oriented MORL, offline linear scalarization, and OptiDICE does not substantively change.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory rewrites, expanded implementation prose, new acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, and insertion of Appendix H with the previous H relabeled I. Most scientific prose and the main section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 4, updates the comparator legends in Figures 4–5, expands several displayed constraints, and reflows existing material, including Figure 8. The retained plots and tables are largely preserved rather than replaced by new displays.

improvement.justification: The new filtering experiment makes dependence on balanced demonstrations more assessable, while explicit computational formulas and a repository pointer improve reproducibility. These are limited gains: Table 4 leaves its uncertainty statistic undefined, the robustness interpretation overlooks the expert MO-Walker2d decline, and an intermediate derivation introduces a utility-sign inconsistency. The unchanged final objective and retained main evidence limit the impact of that error.
